name: arxiv-theorem-5-unavoidable-interleaving
description: The counterexample proving no algorithm can satisfy both forward and backward non-interleaving. Every permitted order interleaves 'de' with 'fg'.

expected.rationale: arXiv Thm 5 / Appendix B: forward non-interleaving forces a < b < (d,f) < (e,g) < c, whose four permitted orders ALL interleave de with fg, while backward non-interleaving would demand defg or fgde. This trace exists to pin that FugueMax lands in the permitted set - it must NOT be 'fixed' by demanding contiguity, which is provably unachievable here.
